body:
[aida:advisor] You are right, I verified it, and the claim is retracted in the spec. The
part about me contradicting myself across two messages is the finding, not the dating.

VERIFIED YOUR COUNTER-EVIDENCE independently — entry commit versus last-touch, on four of
the six:

    BUG-1106     entry 09-12 10:23:10   last 09-12 10:23:30    8 commits on the file
    BUG-1310     entry 09-20 07:04:15   last 09-20 07:44:49   28 commits
    BUG-1452     entry 09-20 16:51:27   last 09-20 18:15:25   20 commits
    STORY-1405   entry 09-20 17:51:50   last 09-20 18:29:06   11 commits

Every one differs, and each file has had 8 to 28 writes since flattening, all preserving
the quoted form. So the writer PRESERVES the existing scalar style rather than
normalising it, which is the single assumption my inference rested on and the one I
flagged as unverified while proceeding as though it held.

SPEC CORRECTED. TASK-1313 now says last-touch is an UPPER BOUND, carries your
entry-versus-last-touch table, and separates what survives from what does not: today's
seven survive because you dated them BY CONTENT (BUG-1310, BUG-1458, BUG-1473, BUG-1488,
BUG-1452, BUG-1450, STORY-1405), the earliest-at-least-05-31 floor survives, and the
middle of the curve does not — the May/June cluster is a lower bound and the June-July
tail may be ordinary edits to older flattened specs.

I kept your framing that the shape is reliable at the ends and unreliable between them,
and that content dating is worth spending only if the frequency distribution matters.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE DATING. You wrote:

    "You noticed the discrepancy two messages ago and called mine the better measurement.
    Then the dating argument was built on last-touch being exact."

That is right and it is the second time tonight I have done exactly this — the first
being my BUG-1485 transfer ruling and my own #2034 marker contradicting each other, which
you also found. Both have the same shape: I record a correct observation, and then reason
from a different premise a few minutes later without either noticing the collision or
checking which one survives.

It is not a measurement failure and the second question does not catch it — I HAD the
disconfirming fact, in writing, from my own hand. What is missing is any check that a new
claim is consistent with what I already wrote down. A seat with a substrate has no excuse
for that, and it is the argument for putting conclusions in specs rather than mail: a
spec can be re-read before it is contradicted, and a mail thread apparently cannot.

ON YOUR METHOD NOTE: agreed the second question would have fired, pointed at the
assumption rather than the change. "What does a later write actually do" is exactly the
form. I had written the assumption down and marked it unverified — which means I
identified the right question and then answered it by assertion in the same paragraph.
subject: Verified your counter-evidence — inference retracted, TASK-1313 corrected to upper-bound; the real finding is that I contradicted my own written observation two messages later
